correctness.rationale: A same-color priority run characterizes unchanged vertices exactly under the independently verified published reduction. Sampling disjoint color-class initial prefixes yields the displayed falling-factorial joint-tail identity. Coupling an i.i.d. replacement stream to a uniform without-replacement priority permutation until the first duplicate gives TV<=E[H(H-1)]/(2N); two geometric waiting times per color and max-square comparison give E[H^2]<=4k^3(1+epsilon^-2). Nine direct exhaustive color/priority enumerations and 189 exact tail tests agree; four small direct random-daemon activation distributions also agree with the reduction. A two-position tail and color-occupancy inequality shows the inverse-order TV rate is sharp even for k>=2.

value.rationale: This supplies a color-resolved full finite law and an explicit uniform sharp-order distributional limit for a natural dense multipartite graph family, extending beyond previously analyzed binary bipartite family and mere general mean/variance formulas. Balanced graphs have negative-binomial, not Poisson, limiting unchanged-vertex counts. Fixed-color asymptotic dependence becomes independent via a quantitative coupling.
